overview: Ireland offers \\postgraduate study options\\ for students who want to study \\aerospace engineering, aircraft systems, flight testing, aerodynamics and advanced engineering research\.

faqs.q: \\Q1. Is Ireland good for Aerospace Engineering postgraduates?\\
faqs.a: \\Aeronautical engineering, flight testing, aircraft systems and related engineering research\\ are fields that may make Ireland an option for students. However, the choice of dedicated Aerospace master's programs is more limited than in some countries, so look carefully at the exact course options.

faqs.q: \\Q2. What are the relevant postgraduate courses available?\\
faqs.a: The University of Limerick offers an MSc in Aeronautical Engineering. SETU offers an MEng in Flight Test Engineering and the University of Galway offers an associated MSc in Wind Energy Engineering. These courses have different specializations and should not be treated as equivalents.

faqs.q: \\Q3. What is the duration of a postgraduate engineering course?\\
faqs.a: \\Many full-time engineering masters programs are about one year long.\\ Check how long that particular program is, including the research project or other requirements.

faqs.q: \\Q4. Can Aerospace Engineering PG be pursued by Mechanical Engineering Graduates?
faqs.a: Some related programs also accept \\graduates of mechanical engineering. But it is contingent upon the university and the course. Check the requirements for \ aerodynamics , mechanics , materials and other relevant subjects .

faqs.q: \\Q5. What types of jobs are available after a postgraduate course?\\
faqs.a: The positions that can be taken up are \\aeronautical engineer, aircraft structures engineer, flight test engineer, aerodynamics engineer, simulation engineer and research engineer. Chances depend on your qualifications, technical skills, employer demands and prevailing work-permission rules.
